scope: Resolve the open question. Original hypothesis (FUN_0089EB40 / FUN_0089E320 are uncataloged sibling receiver applies sharing the chat text-parser with SendLogReceiver) is REFUTED by decomp. The 6 uncataloged callers of FUN_007906C0 (BCS-Y-1029) are NOT receiver applies - they are mid-pipeline text-render helpers (2) and transactional render wrappers (4). The corrected architectural finding is RICHER than the original hypothesis: FUN_007906C0 is shared across multiple OPCODES via intermediate helpers, not just across receivers in the same family.

method.step1: Pre-decomp catalog check (manifests/symbols.json grep): FUN_0089EB40, FUN_0089E320, FUN_00790AA0, FUN_00790B20, FUN_00790A30, FUN_00790BA0 all uncataloged. RTTI scan for *MessageReceiver / *NoticeReceiver / *NotificationReceiver candidates returned ZERO hits in rtti_extraction_OUR.txt.
method.step2: Ghidra batch decomp via tools/ghidra/run_c26_sibling_receivers_decomp.bat -> tools/ghidra/logs/c26_sibling_receivers_decomp.txt (7 functions: the 6 uncataloged callers + SendLogReceiver::apply FUN_0089FBF0 for template comparison).
method.step3: Structural comparison against SendLogReceiver::apply template. SendLogReceiver::apply (1092B, sole caller FUN_00759FD0 dispatch_wrapper) has: full receiver-state init with FUN_00cc7510 SEH cookie helper, switch on packet header byte at param_1+0x10 (cases 0/1/2/0xff), RTDynamicCast checks against ActorBase/CharaBase/WorldMaster RTTI type descriptors, and direct vtable dispatch to text-render UI helpers. NONE of the 6 uncataloged functions match this shape - they are simpler (111-313B), have non-dispatch callers, and don't invoke RTDynamicCast or receiver-state-init helpers.
method.step4: Caller-chain attribution. Traced each uncataloged function to its caller(s) and matched against the existing catalog: FUN_0089EB40 <- FUN_00895A30 (BCS-Y-0432 EventStartStateMachine, opcode 0x012D) + FUN_00893DA0 (uncataloged); FUN_0089E320 <- FUN_0089E3F0 (uncataloged, references CommandUpdaterBase RTTI string); FUN_00790AA0 <- FUN_00774AD0 (BCS-Y-1019 ActorRecordApply_Case0xCC_Primary, opcode 0x00CC) + 2 others; FUN_00790A30 <- FUN_008A0190 (UserDataReceiver::apply, opcode 0x0133 per BCS-Y-0155 + BCS-Y-0595); FUN_00790B20 <- no static callers (orphan or vtable-only); FUN_00790BA0 <- FUN_006F5260 (uncataloged).
method.step5: Three confirmed cross-opcode bindings: 0x012D EventStart, 0x00CC ActorRecord, 0x0133 UserData. None of these opcodes need new matrix attribution (already covered); the new BCS-Y entries are pipeline-helper cross-refs added to existing bcsYIds lists.

key_findings: HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: FUN_0089EB40 and FUN_0089E320 are NOT receiver applies. FUN_0089EB40 is a 238-byte per-buffer-entry text-render helper that iterates param_1+8/+0xc buffer state and invokes FUN_007906C0 once; FUN_0089E320 is a 193-byte indicator-character builder that writes a single byte to *param_2 based on buffer state and references the s___AVCommandUpdaterBase_Command_C string descriptor. Neither has the SendLogReceiver::apply structural shape (receiver-state init, RTDynamicCast, vtable dispatch). Their callers are not LuaActorImpl::vftable[N] dispatch wrappers.

RICHER FINDING: FUN_007906C0 (BCS-Y-1029) is shared across MULTIPLE OPCODES via intermediate helpers, not just across receivers in the SendLog family. Confirmed bindings: 0x0157..0x016A SendLog (direct via SendLogReceiver::apply BCS-Y-0251), 0x012D EventStart (via FUN_0089EB40 helper, called from EventStartStateMachine BCS-Y-0432), 0x00CC ActorRecord (via FUN_00790AA0 wrapper, called from ActorRecordApply_Case0xCC_Primary BCS-Y-1019), 0x0133 UserData (via FUN_00790A30 wrapper, called from UserDataReceiver::apply per BCS-Y-0155 + BCS-Y-0595).

The 4 FUN_00790aa0/b20/a30/ba0 functions form a TRANSACTIONAL WRAPPER family - each one wraps FUN_007906C0 with FUN_00793xxx-setup and FUN_00792xxx-cleanup. Body sizes 111-313 bytes. Three of them have distinct setup/cleanup pairs (FUN_00793190+FUN_00792590, FUN_00793210+FUN_00792710, FUN_00793110+FUN_00792510); FUN_00790BA0 is the largest (313B) with buffer iteration and per-byte-value branching on local_14 ('\a'/'\b'/default) similar to the parser's own state machine.

FUN_00790B20 has NO static callers in Ghidra analysis - likely reached only via vtable indirection or orphaned. Cataloged with confidence=hypothesis-strong (vs confirmed for the other 3 which have direct cross-ref evidence).

Architectural implication for live capture: the 'shared chat-render surface' finding from the chat-render-helper-consolidation pass should be re-framed as the 'shared chat-render PIPELINE' - the parser surface is reached by multiple opcode handlers via two layers of helpers (mid-pipeline + transactional wrappers), not just by sibling receiver classes. World-channel chat receivers (PrivateChat/PartyChat/LinkshellChat) likely use the same parser via additional helper layers that are outside this codebase's Map-channel pcap corpus.
